turns.content: I just finished The Brothers Karamazov. It took me six months but I finally got there.
That's a real achievement — it's a long and demanding read. What did you think?
Incredible. The Grand Inquisitor section is one of the best things I've ever read.
It really is extraordinary — those few chapters could stand alone as a philosophical novella. Did Alyosha work for you as a character?
At first I found him a bit flat compared to Ivan and Dmitri. By the end I understood he was the moral centre.
That's a common journey with him. Dostoevsky hides his depth. Are you going to read more of his work?
I'm thinking Crime and Punishment next, though I might need a break for something lighter first.
A sensible plan. Crime and Punishment is more tightly plotted — different pace entirely.
